evidence: Receiving DO2 minimum ≈7.05 mg/L (t=26.6 h), current ≈9.9 mg/L, far above 2 mg/L constraint
Receiving P: 0.0 g/L at 24 h, 1.01 g/L at 36 h, 2.89 g/L at 48 h — matches source-batch ramp (sources: 2.98–3.06 g/L at 48 h)
All three source batches peaked ~8.0–8.4 g/L at 72 h then plateaued/declined — receiving is on the same healthy trajectory pre-peak
DO2 pattern in receiving (24–28 h dip, feed-event recovery at t=28/40/75 h) is consistent across all sources and receiving, indicating normal process dynamics
submission.rationale: Receiving batch tracks source batches 1–3 closely in both DO2 (never below ~7 mg/L, far above the 2 mg/L minimum) and product kinetics (P=2.89 g/L at 48 h vs 2.98–3.06 g/L in sources). Cultures are mid-production ramp toward a ~72 h peak; feed reductions would sacrifice product mass and increased aeration is unnecessary given ample DO headroom. Normal case — no intervention.
submission.uncertainty: Product assays lag 4 h (latest is P(48 h)); hidden receiving parameters may shift peak timing/level relative to sources. However, DO has >5x headroom over the constraint in real time, so risk of oxygen-limitation violation under KEEP is low.

evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52 h = 9.94 mg/L, ~5x the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Receiving P(48h)=2.89 g/L, within source-batch range 2.98-3.06 g/L
Receiving DO2 trajectory parallels source-1/2/3 (26-28 h dip with full recovery to 10.5-11.5 mg/L)
Product rising steeply (1.0 -> 2.9 g/L between 36 h and 48 h assays), indicating healthy production
submission.rationale: The receiving batch tracks the three source batches within normal batch-to-batch variability: DO2 ~9.9 mg/L at 52 h (far above the 2.0 mg/L minimum, trajectory analogous to sources), and product P(48h)=2.89 g/L matches the source range (2.98-3.06 g/L). There is no oxygen stress, no growth/product deficit, and no anomalous state, so no intervention is needed; feed reduction or aeration changes would risk product mass for no benefit, and stop yields zero counted production.
submission.uncertainty: Receiving DO2 runs ~0.5-1.5 mg/L below source levels in later hours; if this widening continued it could indicate mild OTR deficit, but the margin above the 2.0 mg/L constraint is large. Product assay is 4 h delayed, so current P is extrapolated from the 48 h value. Hidden receiving parameters could differ from source; forward-model predictions were not needed given healthy margins, adding modest residual uncertainty.
